verdicts.reason: A3 fails: the brief requires one trigger, one trick and a stated quiet case, but the done-when only checks that positive prompts match and wrong-task prompts do not; nothing checks for a single trigger or a written quiet case (those appear only under forbidden).

All rules hold: the test script's exit code covers a lifecycle bind, exit 2 blocking a case where the model would have continued, and a clean exit 0, and the brief rates it reliable. The script path .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py was taken as claimed and not checked under the read limits.
A1 fails: the episode-blob guard depends on a 'short body' with no length threshold, so jq -e has no exact limit to test and the blob check comes down to a judgment.

A3 fails: the brief says a tamper attempt fails and the agent gets no delete on its own record, but the done-when admits that tail edits and truncation (in effect a delete) are not caught, and it never checks that the agent has no write or delete path.

A3 fails because the done-when lets 'tokens or seconds dropped' stand in for publishing the token count and never checks that only one harness piece changed. A5 fails because checkRunnable is true while tool is 'none' and the held-out runner with token meter is listed as absent, so no program produces heldout_pass today.
